methodology_audit_note: CRITICAL CORRECTION TO PLAN ASSUMPTIONS: The Appendix contains NO discussion of qualitative-research methodology. It is purely a descriptive game-profile of WoW and Planetside written 'for the sake of readers who have not experienced the games firsthand' (line 6471). Calleja's actual methodology (semi-structured two-session in-game interviews with 25 experienced players recruited in-game, focus groups, machinima review, blog/forum monitoring, iterative coding between interviews) is described in CHAPTER 4 (lines ~1214–1249), NOT in the Appendix. The plan's expectation of methodology + WoW + Planetside as three deliverable elements should be revised in Phase 2: the Appendix delivers two elements (WoW profile + Planetside profile), with the methodological-seed dimension residing in Chapter 4 and being only indirectly supported by the Appendix's game-profile material.
wow_case_profile_aspects: MMORPG genre identification and pen-and-paper RPG lineage
Topography: Azeroth, 96 regions, two factions (Alliance/Horde), contested areas, aesthetic-over-mimetic terrain design, designed channels (mountains/forests/walls/shores)
Lore: Warcraft RTS trilogy lineage, players' functional disinterest in narrative
Server architecture: thousands of regional clone servers, region-locked
Customization: race/class selection, limited avatar customization, gear-based differentiation, 'you are what you wear'
Mechanics: latency-tolerant queued actions, 3rd-person perspective preference, Tab-targeting, level-gated power
Quest design: deliver/kill-X/find-Y structure; external help-site usage normalized
Griefing and corpse-camping on PvP servers
Limited scope for player-driven world-change: respawning mobs/NPCs/resources
planetside_case_profile_aspects: MMOFPS genre identification, distinguishing combat system (long-range, twitch-based)
Topography: Auraxis, 10 continents + 5 caverns, visually generic, no urban areas, Sanctuary as sole safe zone
Absence of social spaces (no marketplaces/taverns/auction houses); equipment-terminal economy
Lore: three-faction premise (Terran Empire, New Conglomerate, Vanu Sovereignty)
Server architecture: three clone servers (US West, US East, Europe), no regional restrictions
Mechanics: real-time latency-sensitive action, mandatory first-person perspective, environmental effects (rain, light) materially affecting play
Level system rewards specialization (weapon/profession certifications) rather than absolute power
Non-combatant support roles materially rewarded via shared XP
Emergent player-generated events, mass collaboration, persistent territorial conquest, sense of agency
expected_concepts: topography and spatial design in virtual worlds
avatar customization economy ('you are what you wear')

expected_interlocutors_note: ONLY two scholarly citations appear in the Appendix body (Fine 1983; Mackay 2001) — both in the framing discussion of pen-and-paper RPG performance. NO methodologists are cited (Glaser+Strauss, Charmaz, Strauss+Corbin, T.L. Taylor, Boellstorff, Pearce, Steinkuehler, Klastrup do NOT appear here). The plan's expectation of qualitative-research methodologists in this unit is REFUTED — they would appear, if anywhere, in Chapter 4's methodology section. All other intra-Appendix references are to participant interview quotations (Haelvon, Nombril, Inauro, Ananke, Baal, Kumacho) and game-developer ludic citations.
exegetical_anchors_note: Phase 0 cite-check confirms NO exegetical anchors required for layered concepts in this unit. The Appendix is descriptive and case-presentational rather than theoretical.
edge_target_rationale: Full-unit treatment per plan §8 resolution. Despite the methodology-absence correction, the Appendix yields rich edge potential via: (a) WoW-Planetside comparative edges across each subsection axis (genre, topography, lore, customization, mechanics, agency); (b) game-to-concept edges anchoring each game profile to the main book's player-involvement model; (c) participant-quotation evidentiary edges; (d) cross-genre comparator edges to other MMOGs cited.

phase2_special_guidance.methodology_seed_revision: The Appendix is NOT itself the methodological seed. Calleja's qualitative methodology resides in Chapter 4 (lines ~1214–1249 of fulltext: 25 experienced players, two-session semi-structured in-game interviews, focus groups, machinima review, blog/forum monitoring, iterative coding between interviews, model derived from salient themes). For the dissertation's empirical adaptation chapter, the methodological seed is Chapter 4; the Appendix supports that chapter by providing the case-profile depth required to justify a two-game comparative design.
phase2_special_guidance.production_editorial_flag: Mention in Phase 2 .md that Figures 12.1 / 12.2 numbering suggests MIT Press internal treatment as Chapter 12.
phase2_special_guidance.comparative_structuring_note: Each subsection (Genres, Topographies, Lore, Clone Worlds, Customization, Mechanics, closing Planetside synthesis) is built as a WoW-then-Planetside comparison. Edge-extraction should exploit this binary scaffolding.

cross_pipeline_bridge_candidates.bridge_rationale: Even with the methodology-absence correction, the Appendix remains a prominent bridge candidate because (a) it demonstrates how Calleja operationalizes the two-genre comparative scaffold that the dissertation's empirical chapter intends to adapt, (b) the eight comparative axes (genre, topography, lore, server, customization, mechanics, agency, emergent-vs-scripted) provide a directly portable analytic template, and (c) the participant-quotation embedding pattern (using player voices to evidence each comparative claim) is a methodologically transferable move. The Chapter 4 methodology should be bridged jointly with this Appendix.
